output.reason: A 71-year-old with severe right hip pain and inability to bear weight after a fall this morning needs immediate emergency imaging and assessment for hip/femur fracture, and she cannot be safely moved or transported by herself.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 now. After a fall, severe hip pain with inability to put weight on that leg can mean a broken hip, which needs emergency X-rays and treatment today. Stay still where you are; do not try to stand, walk or drive yourself. If you develop chest pain, fainting, confusion, or the leg becomes cold, numb or pale, tell the dispatcher right away.
differential: Pubic ramus fracture or hip dislocation

citations.claim: Hip/groin pain with inability to bear weight after a ground-level fall in an older adult is the classic hip fracture presentation warranting emergency evaluation.
citations.limitation: Fall height and exam findings not reported; diagnosis unconfirmed without imaging.

citations.claim: Occult fractures occur despite normal plain radiographs when a patient cannot bear weight with hip pain after a fall, so in-person imaging pathways are needed.
citations.limitation: No imaging has been done; applies to in-person workup, not remote assessment.
